{{Short description|American applied mathematician (1923-2011)}}
{{Use list-defined references|date=April 2021}}
{{Use dmy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=April 2021}}
'''Elizabeth Hahnemann Cuthill''' (October 16, 1923 – January 11, 2011){{r|wapo}} was an American [[applied mathematics|applied mathematician]] and [[numerical analysis|numerical analyst]] known for her work on [[sparse matrix]] algorithms, on block iterative methods for the numerical approximation of [[differential equation]]s, and on the development of computer simulations of [[nuclear reactor]]s. She was a researcher for the [[United States Navy]] at the [[David Taylor Model Basin]].{{r|taylor}} The [[Cuthill–McKee algorithm]] and reverse Cuthill–McKee algorithm are heuristics for permuting matrices into forms with small [[Band matrix|bandwidth]] and for associated problems in [[graph bandwidth]], named for the work of Cuthill with James McKee.{{r|cmk}}{{ran|C}}

==Education and career==
Cuthill was born on October 16, 1923, in Connecticut, the daughter of Paul Richard Hahnemann and Barbara Baumann Hahnemann.{{r|wapo}}

She earned a master's degree in applied mathematics at [[Brown University]] in 1946, with a master's thesis "On the velocity distribution and stability of flow through a two-dimensional channel" supervised by [[Chia-Chiao Lin]].{{r|brown}} After this, she completed a Ph.D. at the [[University of Minnesota]] in 1951; her dissertation, ''Integrals on Spaces of Functions which are Real and Continuous on Finite and Infinite Intervals'', was supervised by [[Robert Horton Cameron]].{{r|mg}} While completing her doctorate, she became an instructor at [[Purdue University]].{{r|purdue}} In 1953, she became a researcher for the [[United States Navy]], working at the [[David Taylor Model Basin]], where she became Numerical Analysis Coordinator for the Computation, Mathematics, and Logistics Department.{{r|taylor}}

She died on January 11, 2011, in [[Frederick, Maryland]].{{r|wapo}}

==Recognition==
Cuthill was named a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 1963.{{r|aaas}} In 1976, she won the David W. Taylor Award of the US Navy "for her valuable contributions in the development and exploitation of mathematical and computational techniques for significant Navy applications".{{r|taylor}}
